raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Icebox Pie
raw_recipe.description: This chilled lemon icebox pie has a deliciously sweet, creamy, and tangy filling made with condensed milk, cream cheese, lemon juice, and lemon zest.

video.description: A favorite dessert when a no-bake, fast pie is needed. Refreshing lemon and sweet cream cheese layered on top of graham cracker crust is an absolute delight. Enjoy at a party or make just because! Add extra beauty by garnishing with whipped cream and mint leaves.

review.reviewBody: We loved this, but I did modify it just a little. I only had 8 oz cream cheese, so I folded about a cup of Cool Whip into the mix. I also used the juice of 1 lemon and 1 lime. Added 1 teaspoon of vanilla and 1/4 teaspoon orange extract. The recipe I normally use for lemon icebox pie only calls for condensed milk and lemon juice, but I like this recipe better, because I believe the cream cheese tones down the flavor of the condensed milk. We really enjoyed the creaminess and light lemon taste.

Disappointing. I thought two packages of cream cheese would be too much and I should have followed my instincts instead of the reviews (and made the other Lemon Icebox Pie recipe on this site that calls for only ONE package of cream cheese, darn it) Too cream cheesey tangy, not sweet enough because of it (I'm sure the sweetness level would be fine if only one package of cream cheese was used) and not lemony enough, even tho' I nearly doubled the amount of zest called for. I also made my own crust, using "Graham Cracker Crust," also from this site. It's a pretty pie, but it's not as mouthwatering good as it looks.

Great recipe! Used the graham cracker crust recipe from this website and added 1/2 t. salt just to make it more delicious. We did lightly bake the crust for about 8 minutes and just let it cool to room temp while making the rest. Used light version of cream cheese just because I do this a lot to cut calories and I think it tastes better anyway because it's not as heavy. Ended up using only half of the container of sweetened condensed milk because often a full can is just too sweet for our liking as we have cut down our sugar intake and too sweet just isn't as appetizing as it once was. Half a can was perfect sweetness! Also added a lemon to get more lemon flavor, my lemons were on the small size so i think you just have to taste after two and see if it needs more. I added a teaspoon of vanilla because someone suggested it so I did. Stuck it in the fridge for a couple hours before eating. We topped this on 4th of July with fresh blueberries, strawberries and raspberries. It was sooooooo good! I was lazy and didn't make whipped cream to dollop on top but that would be yummy too. A very simple and super yummy summer treat. Will definitely make again!

I never thought this pie was going to set after pouring it into the crust so i added an addition1/2 block of cream cheese hoping that would help. After a couple hours, it didn't look much better. I then placed it in the freezer and voila, it set beautifully. I used the juice of 3 lemons and added more zest to tone down the cream cheese flavor. Everyone really liked this pie. The only disappointment was that the filling was shallow. Don't give up on this pie. It is delish.

I won our family's holiday dessert competition with this pie! I used 12 ounces of cream cheese, juiced 3 lemons and zested 3 and a half lemons. This was an excellent easy to follow recipe. I made the graham cracker crust from scratch and recommend homemade so you have a thick, crispy, buttery crust for such a great filling. Finally, I added whipped cream and blue berries around the edge of my pie.

Delicious! I added two more lemons because the cream cheese was too overpowering and couldn’t taste anything else. My husband has Celiac so bought a pre made GF Graham cracker crust added 1/2 stick butter and reshaped to pan. Tasted like a regular pie!

Can make this with only 4 ingredients: small can frozen lemonade mix thawed, a can of condensed milk, small tub cool whip. Gently mix it all till well blended, pour into graham or chocolate cookie pie crust, freeze until firm. Yum!

We made this pie and enjoyed it. The second time, we modified it a little bit and it was a big hit with family and friends. Ingredients • 1 (9 inch) prepared graham cracker crust • 2 (8 ounce) packages cream cheese, softened • 1 (14 ounce) can sweetened condensed milk • ¾ cup frozen lemonade concentrate (Adjust according to taste) • 6 tablespoons Monin Blackberry Syrup • 1 teaspoon lemon zest Directions 1. Beat cream cheese in a medium mixing bowl until fluffy. Add condensed milk, lemonade, blackberry syrup, and lemon zest. Mix until smooth. 2. Pour mixture into crust. Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving. Garnish with whipped cream and blackberries.

Great recipe 💜 I made this lemon ice box pie before, but instead of using cool whip for the topping. I separated 2 eggs using the egg whites with 2 teaspoons of sugar and blended them for the lemon ice box pie topping

This recipe was perfect! I had 4 very large lemons. I used the rind of all four and only the juice of 2 lemons. Of course you need to add in increments until you get the perfect taste of lemon. Mine came out light, sweet with just the right amount of lemon taste. I made a graham cracker crust from scratch as well. Great spring/summer dessert. Thanks!
Made this with the juice of 3 lemons and without the crust. I also folded in creamy cool whip to increase volume- I placed a few vanilla wafers on top everyone loved it- will make it again
I made this according to directions, and it was simply divine! Perfect flavor and consistency. It has become a regular in my list of favorites.
It’s my son’s favorite! I make it every Christmas! I do add an extra lemon for the juice and the zest. That to me makes it perfect!

This was fairly easy to make and came out really well! I followed a lot of other reviewers' suggestion and used the juice and zest of 3 lemons which seemed to be a good balance with the cream cheese. I will definitely be making this again!
This is super easy to make but as far as lemon flavor it left a lot to be desired. I'm going to try it one more time but add lemon extract to add more lemon flavor.
Absolutely delicious!!! So easy to make!!!

So delicious and so easy to make! I followed the recipe exactly and left the pie to set overnight. It cut into beautiful neat slices the next day. I will try some of the other suggestions of using either lime juice or a combination of lemon/lime next time.
Delicious and easy to make. Just like many others I changed a few ingredients up to put my own twist on it.
Excellent quick and easy lemon dessert. Followed above directions just added a 1/4 teaspoon of vanilla as others suggested. Everyone loved it and requested I make again.
